mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter is interpreted as a shift toward restrictive policy, which raises the cost of capital and dampens equity valuation growth, thereby predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS average > 4% over the past quarter
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >70% of similar tightening episodes, or the 20-day return exceeds -1% when trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate > 2% AND UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Over a 5-year window, the 60-day forward return is not statistically different from zero when both triggers are present (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% yoy for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates earnings expectations and supports higher equity valuations, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is negative despite sustained demand growth (p-value > 0.05 in a rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% suggests weakening supply-side constraints, which can lead to higher inflation expectations and equity premium demands, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p-value > 0.1) when INDPRO contracts.

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 0.3% while the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains flat, it suggests inflation is outpacing policy lags, prompting investors to demand higher equity returns and pushing 20-day forward S&P 500 returns to the negative.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month increase > 0.3% AND FEDFUNDS change <= 0%
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is non-negative in >50% of similar inflation surprise events (rolling 12-month window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for two consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in jobless claims (PAYEMS), indicates a tight labor market that can fuel wage growth and inflation, thereby depressing equity valuations and predicting negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 2 consecutive months AND PAYEMS < previous month
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (Granger causality p > 0.05) when labor market is tight.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to post-2007 financial normalization (as indicated by FEDFUNDS > 5% for 4 consecutive months) weakens risk premia and allows valuation discounts to fade, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days in normalization regimes.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS average > 5% over past 4 months AND regime condition: 'post-2007 normalization'
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not positive in >80% of historical normalization periods (2008-2020).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, one-time decline in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5 percentage points, followed by a rapid reversal in the next month, creates a 'put option' effect on the dollar and equity markets, pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns to the negative.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > -0.5pp in a single month AND reversal > 0.5pp in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.1) during similar rate shock reversals.
